title: auth GET /api/users/lookup refuses connector tokens, so every Platform-S transfer-custody 401s and falls back to a flat anchor — KS-739's users:read ruling cannot take effect
description:
## BLUF

**No Platform-S rights-assign or rights-reassign reaches** `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` **successfully.** originate resolves `newHolderEmail` by calling auth's `GET /api/users/lookup` with the **caller's** `Authorization` header, and `/lookup` accepts only access tokens (`authenticate()`). Platform-S authenticates per Organisation with a **connector** token, so auth answers 401 *"Invalid token"*, originate passes it through ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)'s 4xx rule), and S degrades to a flat `/api/anchors` anchor. No `custody_events` row is written and `documents.owner_user_id` never moves.

[KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) (Done, archived) ruled 2026-09-02 that *"Platform S provisions* `users:read` *on its connector key; K does not widen* `ALLOWED_LOOKUP_ROLES`*"*. That ruling cannot take effect: the scope check sits behind an authenticator that rejects the token type before any scope is read. A missing scope would answer **403**; what S receives is **401 Invalid token**.

## Code (platform-k `develop` `0736d8b78`)

* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1665-1671` — email-only path: `fetch(${AUTH_SERVICE_URL}/api/users/lookup?email=…, { headers: { Authorization: <caller's header> } })`.
* `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1708-1730` — a 4xx from the lookup is passed through; 401 → *"The credential on this request was rejected by the user lookup. Re-authenticate and retry."* ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)).
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:266` — `userRoutes.get('/lookup', authenticate(), …)` — access tokens only.
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:357-359` — "[KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) *(Option A): this ONE route also accepts a connector token — see authenticateAccessOrConnector. Every other route keeps plain authenticate()."* — `/stub` was widened; `/lookup` was not.
* Platform-S side: `ssd/Services/CardanoAnchor/CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs` `TransferCustodyAsync` sends `{ newHolderEmail, reason }` + `onBehalfOf` with `Authorization: Bearer <connector access token>` (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:1527`).

## Measured — local pair, slot 3, 2026-10-01

platform-s `f370236c` (+ [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) systemTest changes only) ↔ platform-k `0736d8b78`, fresh databases, 33/33 K containers up, `/health/deep` 200, S provisioning key accepted, 10/0/0 organisations registered.

**4 of 4** transfer-custody calls refused, identical body, under Organisation 3's connector key:

```
transfer-custody status=401 body={"success":false,"error":{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"The credential on this request was rejected by the user lookup. Re-authenticate and retry. Upstream said: Invalid token"}} … using /api/anchors fallback.
```

* 09:21:55Z — 2 calls ([PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914)'s date-sort seed: two documents delegated to a same-org colleague).
* 09:22:55–09:31:06Z — 2 calls during `npm run test:k-live` (`verb_matrix.spec.ts` rights-assign + rights-reassign on K document `7af2374a-dd61-47e7-be50-122dcb5e412b`).

In the same window, Organisation 3's connector token **succeeded** on `originate` (201) and on lifecycle events (`rights-unassign`, `delete`) — so the key is valid; only the auth-service lookup refuses it.

## Why nothing went red

The platform-s `@k-live` cell "rights-assign and rights-unassign each reach K" asserted only that the S edge carries an anchor K resolves as not-failed — which the flat fallback also satisfies. It passed (17 passed / 1 skipped) while both custody calls 401'd. [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) tightens that cell to assert the custody transfer K records — `GET /api/documents/{id}` `owner.id` must move off its pre-assign value (measured: it reads `""` before and after today's refused transfers). The cell is **red until this ticket ships**, deliberately, and turns green once K records the transfer. Platform-S's `TransferCustodyAsync` carries a comment naming this ticket.

## Options (Kamil's call — no K code changed)

1. **Widen** `/lookup` **to** `authenticateAccessOrConnector()`, as [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) did for `/stub` — makes [KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the)'s `users:read` ruling effective (the connector key then needs that scope).
2. **originate resolves the holder with its own service credential**, not the caller's header — removes the dependency on the caller's token type.
3. **Platform-S sends** `newHolderId` — requires S to know the K user id of the recipient (S-side; it does not today).

Whichever is chosen, a recipient with no K account still gets the typed 404 `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` ([KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) measurement A) — worth confirming the S holder exists in K once the 401 is gone.

## Related

[KS-739](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-739/transfer-custody-maps-a-401403-from-userslookup-to-502-bad-gateway-the) (Done, archived — ruling this ticket shows cannot take effect) · [KS-564](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-564/share-lifecycle-events-and-certificationsissue-all-fail-on-recipient) (Option A connector scoping) · [PS-681](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-681/systemtest-k-live-every-share-and-rights-verb-times-out-waiting-for) (Done — Stuart's original 502 report) · [PS-992](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-992/systemtest-the-date-sort-contract-has-asserted-nothing-since-ps-914) (platform-s: the k-live cell that hid this).

nodes.title: Refs KS-1402: a transfer-custody recipient K does not know is minted as an invited stub, not refused
Refs KS-1402: a Platform-S custody transfer whose holder resolves is recorded, not a 500
KS 1402: originate resolves a transfer-custody holder email itself
KS-1402: accept a connector token on the users lookup route

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Yes, Kintsugi wrote one custody event for every accepted call: seven events for your document, at the seven times you listed, to the second. The document's owner moved to a single invited user that Kintsugi created 32 ms before the first event. None of the seven events recorded an anchor. I cannot confirm that the invited user's address is firsttime@lhsg.com, and I cannot show the reason for the refused anchors, for the two reasons under "Not measured".

All times are UTC, with AEDT (UTC+11) in brackets. Each figure says how it was read. Sections 1 to 3 are from SELECTs on Kintsugi on 29 Oct between 04:53 and 05:01 UTC [15:53 and 16:01 AEDT], in read-only database sessions. Section 4 is from the box's REVISION records, read at 05:04 UTC [16:04 AEDT].

**1. The invited user**
- Kintsugi holds one user created inside the 26 Oct 03:00 to 03:20 UTC window: status `invited`, role `user`, created 2026-10-26 03:09:24.532 [14:09:24 AEDT], in Kintsugi's default tenant. It was created 32 ms before the first custody event.
- It is the recipient of all seven events and the owner of the document now. It owns no other document.
- Its address is not shown here. See "Not measured".

**2. The custody events** (the K document you name, `427c4864-fde0-4713-9e36-7e50d0097a49`, is stored on Kintsugi as the document's external id)

| # | created (UTC) | [AEDT] | from | to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2026-10-26 03:09:24.564 | [14:09:24] | none | the invited user |
| 2 | 03:10:24.746 | [14:10:24] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 3 | 03:11:24.832 | [14:11:24] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 4 | 03:12:24.896 | [14:12:24] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 5 | 03:13:25.046 | [14:13:25] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 6 | 03:14:25.113 | [14:14:25] | the invited user | the invited user |
| 7 | 03:15:25.262 | [14:15:25] | the invited user | the invited user |

- Count: 7, all inside 03:09:00 to 03:16:00 UTC; the gaps between them are 60, 60, 60, 60, 60 and 60 seconds. Control on the same query: the 28 Oct document from your KS-1384 table has 1 event. So events 2 to 7 are repeats of the same transfer: each wrote a row that moves the document from the invited user to the same user.
- Ownership: the document's owner is the invited user. That user did not exist before 03:09:24.532 on 26 Oct and the document was created on 23 Oct 09:10, so the owner changed in this window. The document's `updated_at` is 03:15:25.262, the time of event 7, and its status is still `draft`.
- All seven events have an empty "transferred by" and an empty anchor transaction. The provenance table holds seven `transfer-custody` rows for the document, first 03:09:24 and last 03:15:25.
- Kintsugi's audit trail holds seven `POST …/transfer-custody` requests answered 201, at the same seven times.

**3. The anchors**
- Kintsugi's audit trail holds seven `POST /api/anchors` requests answered 400, each 8 to 37 ms after a transfer-custody request. Those seven are the only `anchors.create` requests answered 400 in the trail, which begins on 20 Aug (7 of its 12 `anchors.create` rows). The trail records no error text for them.
- Kintsugi's anchor table holds 0 rows for this document; control: 1 row for the 28 Oct document.
- So no anchor was created for any of the seven transfers, and the transfer route answered success each time. From the audit trail alone I cannot tell whether those 400s are the calls S made after each transfer or the route's own internal call; their timing fits the calls S made.

**4. Which build**
Kintsugi ran develop `1ae6f17d19a8` for all seven events (deployed 26 Oct 00:46:20 UTC [11:46:20 AEDT], replaced 26 Oct 07:55:24 UTC [18:55:24 AEDT], read from the box's REVISION records). Your comment names `bcc51903d`, which was the build before that. Kintsugi now runs `5dccdcb29ec2`.

**Not measured**
- Whether the invited user's address is firsttime@lhsg.com (as you gave it). Kintsugi stores addresses encrypted. Its address-lookup column did not match a plain hash of a known address in a control test, so I could not search by address without decrypting, and I did not decrypt.
- The reason for the refused anchors, and whether the transfer route's own anchor call also met a 400 `Invalid DID`. Originate's log on Kintsugi starts on 29 Oct 01:05:59 UTC [12:05:59 AEDT], after later redeploys, and no file on the box holds 26 Oct log lines. The "Lifecycle anchor emission failed" and "Custody transferred" lines for 26 Oct are therefore not available.

Update, 03:17 UTC: **S stopped the loop at 03:15:58 UTC.** The transfer for document `427c4864-fde0-4713-9e36-7e50d0097a49` reached Kintsugi **7 times**, at 03:09:24, 03:10:24, 03:11:24, 03:12:24, 03:13:25, 03:14:25 and 03:15:25 UTC, each answered 2xx with no anchor reference. Nothing more will arrive from S for it. On Stuart's instruction S's row was given a local marker and parked. A count of `custody_events` for that document over 03:09–03:16 UTC would show whether K wrote one row per call. The S fix is filed on the S side. For context, that document's own upload on 23 Oct 09:10 UTC (same Entra-verified actor) was created on K, but its anchor was refused for the same `did:jwk` reason, and S parked it as FAILED.

@kamil.kreiser — **live custody transfer on dev-ps against Kintsugi `bcc51903d`, 26 Oct 2026 03:09 UTC: K accepted it, but returned no anchor reference.** Read from S's side (dev-ps app log and its `DocumentTransaction` row; S develop `4fb15e7`).

- **What ran:** stuart@obeden.com assigned S document 15 (K document `427c4864-fde0-4713-9e3…`) to firsttime@lhsg.com, a person who had never received custody or a certification, so K had no user for them. S row 96, chain id `5008820d82c743fd971cbc4d99729a20`.
- **K's answer to `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody`: 2xx**, with no `transfer.anchorId` / `transfer.anchor.id` in the body. S logged `transfer-custody OK but no ref in payload for tx 5008820d…; using /api/anchors fallback`. So the old 404 `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` and the 500 are gone on Kintsugi. **Please confirm from your side:** an invited stub for firsttime@lhsg.com in `users`, and the `custody_events` row(s) with the owner moved.
- **Why no anchor reference, as far as S can tell:** the assigner is Entra-verified, so S's identity block carries a `did:jwk` `actorDid`. S's flat fallback (`POST /api/anchors`) was then refused 400 `Invalid DID — expect did:key:… or did:web:…` at `identity.actorDid` (the KS-1175 widening). That suggests the custody route's own anchor call met the same 400 and the route returned success without it, the same shape as KS-1709 on certify. Can you confirm from originate's log?
- **The S-side problem this exposes, which matters for your tables:** S's background drain re-sends any row that has no K reference on every pass, with no limit. For this row it has re-sent the same transfer-custody **once a minute: 03:09:24, 03:10:24, 03:11:24 …, 4 calls by 03:13 UTC**, each answered 2xx by K and each followed by a refused flat anchor. If K writes a `custody_events` row per call, Kintsugi is accumulating one duplicate transfer a minute for this document. A count of `custody_events` for that document would tell us. It continues until S stops it (I'm asking Stuart now) or K accepts `did:jwk`. It is the only row in that state on dev-ps.

The S fix (do not re-send a side-effecting verb K has already accepted; park the row instead) will be an S ticket.

**#1620 measured end to end, 19 Oct 12:13–12:31Z, slot 4, K develop `115797747` (fresh DB, 54 migrations), S develop `b7d414b`:** the PS-992 cell's rights-assign to `firsttwo@lhsg.com` — a person this K had never seen — now answers **201**: S logs `'rights-assign' → transfer-custody ref anchor_ff9fea6c-…`, K's `users` gains one **invited** stub (2 → 3), `custody_events` holds 1 row with `transferred_by_id` NULL, and originate's log has no 22P02 beyond its startup probe. Zero `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` in the run. The cell then fails on its custodian read-back (`GET /api/documents/{id}` → 404 to the k-live client after ownership moved), the shape already filed to Peter on PS-1299 — so on this build the transfer half is green and the read half is the estate's.

On PS-1091 reading Canceled: that was done **because** the K side changed, not on the assumption it would not — it was cancelled at 09:55Z quoting Kam's (a) verbatim, with the note that #1620 makes S's pre-transfer stub call unnecessary and that Kintsugi keeps answering 404 until it takes #1614 + #1620 together. No second look needed; the S-side residue is the closer cell's read-back (PS-1299, Peter).

Read #1620 merged at `a0da739b6` and KS-1662's fix at `115797747`. Stuart's slot-1 K was rebuilt at `115797747` today (originate image 11:34Z carries the stub path), so the next S run against it will exercise the mint for real; the dev-ps pairing stays as you describe — 201 locally, 404 on Kintsugi — until the round.

## BLUF

**The invited-stub holder is merged — not deployed.** PR #1620 landed on `develop` at
`a0da739b6954d42333640ea190d877f031803c7f`. A custody transfer naming a recipient Platform K has
never seen now **mints an invited stub user and records the transfer**, instead of answering
`404 RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND`. That completes the build half of Kam's ruling. **Nothing is live**, so
Platform S still sees the old 404 on every environment until a deploy round carries this.

## Recommendation

1. **Deploy needs a rebuild, and both KS-1402 changes should travel together** — the 500 fix with
   migration `052` (merged earlier at `80868551e679`) and this stub holder. A box with one and not
   the other is a state no suite covers. Rebuilding **either** the `migrations` image **or** the
   `api-gateway` image lands `052`; afterwards check `custody_events.transferred_by_id` reads
   `is_nullable = YES` — the runner prints `applied=N failed=0` even when it ran a stale image, so
   the column is the evidence, not the summary line.
2. **This ticket stays In Progress** until it is deployed and live-checked.
3. One follow-up is open and worth doing before anyone leans on the tenant guarantees: **KS-1662**.

## Detail

**What landed.** On the email path's zero-row case only, the route calls auth's
`POST /api/users/stub` with the caller's credential forwarded — the shape `certifications/issue`
already used for `holderEmail`, which is the precedent Kam's card names. auth stays the only writer
of `users`, so its PII encryption, the email lookup hash, the cross-tenant rule and the
claim-on-registration flow are not duplicated. **No auth change, no new scope, no migration**:
Platform S's connector key already passes that endpoint's gate.

**What is deliberately different from Kintsugi.** Kintsugi answers 404 for an unknown recipient;
Platform K now answers 201. Recorded separately on this ticket with a case-by-case table — only that
one branch diverges.

**Gaps in the shipped coverage, stated rather than left to be discovered (KS-1662):**
- The route's **tenant predicates are not independently proven**. `users` is FORCE RLS for the
  application role, so dropping a predicate still leaves the suite green — RLS hides the row anyway.
  A cell without RLS is needed before anyone treats those predicates as tested.
- The non-2xx fallback has no cell (it fails safe).
- Two code comments name an auth test as a scope tripwire; it is not one. The real tripwire is an
  api-gateway test. Corrected in the PR body; the comments are in KS-1662.

**Review.** Tier-1 gated twice. Round 1 returned NO GO on two blockers — the race fallback was
written for a database constraint that does not exist, so it could never run in the real race, and
the tenant re-read had no cell on the branch where auth skips its own tenant check. Both fixed, each
with a cell that reds without the fix, and the gate's own mutant now reds the new cell. Round 2
returned GO, and the landed tree equals the figure predicted before the merge.

**Also noted:** PS-1091 — the Platform-S ticket for this 404 — now reads **Canceled**. If that was
done on the assumption the K side would not change, it is worth a second look now that it has.

Read, 19 Oct 10:00 UTC: #1614 merged (`80868551e`), Kam's ruling (a) — **K creates the invited stub on transfer, as `certifications/issue` does** — and the divergence table. Three S consequences, recorded on the S side:

1. **PS-1091 (S stubs the holder first) is withdrawn** — the ruling makes it unnecessary; the ticket is cancelled with the ruling quoted.
2. **The PS-992 closer cell will pass on a K at or after #1620 for its transfer** — and then still needs its custodian read-back fixed (my comment above; filed to Peter on PS-1299), so a red there after #1620 is the read, not the transfer.
3. **Deploy pairing noted:** #1614 (migration 052) and #1620 ship together, and until Kintsugi takes them a rights-assign to a new person succeeds locally and 404s on dev-ps; S's dev-ps proof (PS-1284) will state which build it ran against.

One privacy fact for KS-1655, posted there: S's person erasure already sends K a `POST /api/gdpr/erasures`, so the retention question for S-minted stubs is whether that erasure reaches an `invited` row.

## BLUF

**Platform K now deliberately diverges from Kintsugi on one answer, and it will stay diverged until
Kintsugi takes this build.** For a custody transfer naming a recipient email with no Platform K
user: **Kintsugi answers `404 RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND`; Platform K `develop` answers `201`**, minting an
invited stub holder. This is Kam's ruling, not a defect — recording it because "Kintsugi still
answers the correct 404" was load-bearing evidence earlier on this ticket, and a future reader
comparing the two boxes will otherwise read the difference as a regression.

## Recommendation

Treat the divergence as expected until a Kintsugi deploy round carries this change. Two
consequences worth holding:

1. **The deploy order now matters in the other direction.** Earlier on this ticket the risk was that
   a Kintsugi round would make Platform S *worse*. It is now the reverse: Platform K leads, and
   Kintsugi keeps refusing these transfers until it is updated.
2. **Two things ship together or the gap widens**: the KS-1402 500 fix (merged, `80868551e679`, with
   migration 052) and the invited-stub build (**PR #1620**, at review, head `dbb00e65dfb0`). A box
   with one and not the other is a state neither suite covers.

## Detail

**What changed, measured.** The old answer was pinned by a cell that passed:
`KINTSUGI — a connector naming a holder K does NOT know still answers 404 RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND and
writes nothing`. It has been rewritten and renamed rather than deleted, and it keeps its
writes-nothing assertions.

**The divergence is exactly one branch, not a behaviour change across the route:**

| Case | Kintsugi | Platform K after this build |
|---|---|---|
| Recipient email has a K user in this tenant | 201 | 201 (unchanged) |
| Recipient email has **no** K user | **404 `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND`** | **201** + an INVITED stub minted |
| Recipient email belongs to **another** tenant | 404 | 404 (unchanged) |
| Unknown `newHolderId` (by id, not email) | 404 | 404 (unchanged) |
| Malformed email | 400 | 400 (unchanged) |

**Authority:** Kam, card `secuura-ks1402-who-creates-the-holder-1019` = (a), 2026-10-19:
*"K creates an invited stub user on transfer. As certifications/issue already does for holderEmail."*

**What it means for anyone measuring the two boxes.** A rights-assign to a brand-new person will
succeed against Platform K and 404 against Kintsugi. Neither is broken; they are at different
commits. The S-side ticket for the 404 itself is PS-1091.

**Not deployed.** Nothing has been run against either deployed box for this work — the readings
above are from code and from local suites, not from the live boxes.

**Measured before the merge, as offered: #1614 (`ddd54b836`) fixes the 500, and K now records S's custody transfers.** Slot 4, 19 Oct 07:16–08:44 UTC: K built from a local branch = develop `722e07f19` + #1613 + #1614 (`f5c6c0ff2`), fresh database, migration 052 applied (54 of 54); the running originate image carries the new actor helper. S develop `2c1d179`, fresh database, `PII_LOOKUP_HMAC_KEY` present on originate.

**Where the holder resolves (a person K already knows as a user or INVITED stub), the transfer now succeeds:**
- Five S `rights-assign` events during the full suite went through `POST /{id}/transfer-custody` and came back with a custody anchor (`'rights-assign' → transfer-custody ref anchor_…` at 08:14:32, 08:15:05, 08:19:50, 08:23:01, 08:35:29Z) — no flat-anchor fallback.
- K's `custody_events` holds **5 rows, `transferred_by_id` NULL on all 5** — exactly the "resolved user, else NULL" the fix specifies for S's people; `documents.owner_user_id` moved (e.g. document `81aec073-…` → owner `8802e2e2-…` at 08:35:29Z).
- originate log since the run began: **0 × `22P02`, 0 × "Failed to transfer custody"** (the only 22P02 in the whole log is a startup probe with the literal `test-123`, before any S traffic).

**Where the holder is unknown to K, the answer is still 404 `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND`, before the insert** — 22 such refusals in the run, all for S people with no K user. That is the holder-stub decision still with Kam (K mints the INVITED stub on transfer, or S stubs first via `POST /api/users/stub` = PS-1091). The PS-992 cell (`verb_matrix` rights-assign) stays red on this slot for that reason: its holder, `firsttwo@lhsg.com`, has no stub on a fresh K.

**One new shape for the spec, not for #1614:** in the full run that cell's holder did resolve (a stub from an earlier spec), the transfer succeeded, and the cell then failed on its *read-back* — `GET /api/documents/{id}` for the custodian answered **404** to the k-live client after ownership moved to the stub user (the spec's own hint: "tenant-scoped — is this the same tenant?"). So once #1614 deploys, the closer cell needs its custodian read to survive a successful transfer; filed on the S side for Peter.

Evidence files: S app log and `custody_events` reads on slot 4; full suite 2,862 / 3 / 163, S restarts 0. Nothing deployed.

**Kam has ruled who creates the holder: K does, as an invited stub user, on transfer.**

Kam's words, verbatim:

> K creates an invited stub user on transfer

Card `secuura-ks1402-who-creates-the-holder-1019`, option **(a)**. Ruled on the live board 2026-10-19 between 18:22 and 18:23 AEDT; recorded 18:28.

Shape, per the card:

- It works the way `certifications/issue` already does for `holderEmail` — so this follows an existing K pattern rather than introducing a new one.
- It is a **K build with a tier-1 gate**: a user row created from a connector call, so the tenant boundary and the PII handling both have to be proved, not asserted.
- **Platform S changes nothing.**

Sequencing: this is the next build after #1614 lands. **Nothing is built by this comment** — it records the ruling only.

## BLUF

**The 500 is fixed and merged — not deployed.** PR #1614 landed on `develop` at
`80868551e67934cb951d28eec44ce3bdf835944c` (squash of `ddd54b836394`, parent `31cfb44dce84`).
A Platform-S custody transfer whose holder resolves is now recorded instead of answering
`500 INTERNAL_ERROR "Failed to transfer custody"`. **Nothing is live yet**, so Platform S will
still see the 500 on any environment until the deploy below happens.

## Recommendation

Two things, in order:

1. **Deploy is a rebuild, not a config change.** Migration `052` ships *inside an image*, so
   rsyncing the `.sql` does nothing on its own. Rebuilding **either** the `migrations` image **or**
   the `api-gateway` image lands it — the api-gateway image also bundles `migrations/`
   (`services/api-gateway/Dockerfile:75`) and its Stage 1 applies new files from it.
2. **Verify the column afterwards, don't assume the runner.** Check
   `custody_events.transferred_by_id` reads `is_nullable = YES`. The migration runner prints
   `Summary: applied=N failed=0` even when it ran a stale image's migrations, so the printed
   summary is not evidence; the column is.

Nothing changes on the Platform S side. Once this is deployed, the PS-992 rights-assign cell is
the closer.

## Detail
